Percentiles

Each survey's newest reading as a percentile (the number in each dot) of its full history, the last three years and the last year, against a dotted median at 50.
How to read this

A percentile is the share of the history at or below the reading: 96 means only 4% of readings were higher. The first row ranks against every official reading since the survey began; the last two against the last three years and the last year, including the newest weeks, which NAAIM and AAII publish in full only later. Some shares have drifted for decades (AAII neutral from about 41% in the late 1980s to 28% in the 2020s), so a full-history percentile partly measures the drift; a reading that is also extreme over the last year is extreme now. Dots that would overlap are spread apart; the number in each dot is its percentile. Colours match the cards below.

NAAIM exposure

Active managers' average stock exposure as NAAIM reports it each week, from 200% short to 200% long.
How to read this

Three blocks: the last four readings, newest first, each with its percentile since 2006 in brackets and the average since 2006 dashed; each week's change from the week before (green up, red down); and the average since 2006 with the last year's average, high and low. The last-year numbers include the newest weeks, which NAAIM publishes for free only after about three months. The newest reading's percentiles are in the Percentiles card at the top of the page.

AAII votes

The share of AAII members bullish (green), neutral (grey) and bearish (red) on stocks over the next six months.
How to read this

Three blocks: the last four surveys, newest first; the average since 1987 with each vote's highest week in the last year; and each recent week's bulls minus bears against its average since 1987 (dashed), with its percentile since 1987 in brackets. The newest week's percentiles are in the Percentiles card at the top of the page.

AAII asset allocation

AAII members' average split between stocks (green), bonds (blue) and cash (grey), percent of portfolio, monthly.
How to read this

Four blocks: the last four surveys, newest first; the average since 1987 with each share's highest month in the last year; each recent month's stocks share against its average since 1987; and the newest month's shares as percentiles (the number in each dot) of every month since 1987, of the last three years and of the last year (the dotted line is the median). The shares have drifted over the decades, cash from about 33% in the late 1980s to about 17% in the 2020s, so a low cash percentile since 1987 partly reflects the drift. AAII publishes each month in the first days of the next.

Index lookback

Sentiment against price

NAAIM and AAII under SPY, each placed between its own lowest (0) and highest (100) reading of the lookback: above 80 the crowd leans long, below 20 it is washed out.
How to read this

Each line is a survey's 2-week average on that range index. Faint dots: each week as read, on the same scale; the large one is the latest week, read out above the panel with its index. Shaded weeks: SPY below its high so far, amber 5-10%, orange 10-20%, red 20% or more. Opens on 5 years (3 on a phone); the buttons zoom down to 3 months without changing the index.

Weekly columns

AAII allocation against price

SPY above AAII members' monthly split between stocks (green), bonds (blue) and cash (grey) since 1987, and each share against its own prior three years.
How to read this

The middle panel stacks the shares to 100% of portfolio: stocks sit on the floor, so their band's top edge is the stocks share, and the dashed line is its average since 1987. The bottom panel is each share minus its own average over the prior three years, in points. Opens on the whole history (SPY's starts in 1993); the buttons zoom in. Each month is drawn on its last day, about a month before AAII publishes it.

Newest stored observation: SPY 2026-11-13, NAAIM 2026-11-11, AAII 2026-11-12, ES COT 2026-11-03.

Each index places a series' 2-week average between its own lowest (0) and highest (100) reading of the trailing three years. When an old high or low leaves that window the scale shifts under the line, as it does for the COT index.

Every NAAIM point sits on the Friday of the week it became public.

Both surveys mostly follow price: NAAIM's level tracks SPY's trailing 13-week return at 0.62, AAII's at 0.44, so a high reading usually follows a rally. Neither moves with the S&P 500 COT groups (correlations of weekly to quarterly changes near zero, 2006-2026), which is why the commercials row is drawn as a contrast, not a pairing.

Studied once under a pre-registration (npf, 2026-11-05, SPY 13-week forward return, on weekly percentile ranks rather than this index): weeks with NAAIM in its bottom fifth were followed by about 2.5 points more than top-fifth weeks, a marginal lean that did not clear its line, and NAAIM added nothing measurable once S&P speculator positioning was known. Context, not signal.

AAII's Asset Allocation Survey is monthly, from 1987-11: members' average split between stocks, bonds and cash. Each month is dated on its last day and AAII publishes it in the first days of the next, so the newest month here (2026-10) is about a month old by design.

Like the sentiment surveys, the stocks share mostly follows price: placed in its own three-year range it tracks SPY's trailing 12-month return at 0.67, so a high share usually follows a rally. The chart's bottom panel sets each share against its own prior three years in points, not as a 0-100 index: on these slow monthly series an index reads moves of a point or two as extremes. Context, not signal.

Provisional data: NAAIM's newest 13 weeks are read off a StockCharts chart (within about 0.2 points of NAAIM's own values), since NAAIM's free table runs about a quarter behind; AAII's newest 2 weeks are typed from AAII's public results page (bulls minus bears within 0.1 point of the member spreadsheet). Each is replaced by the official value when it is published.

Sources: NAAIM Exposure Index (naaim.org), AAII Sentiment Survey and Asset Allocation Survey (aaii.com), SPY total return, CFTC Commitments of Traders (S&P 500 consolidated). Not investment advice.
